name: Reasoning by Analogy
blurb: Work out the change, then make it happen again.
childIntro: The top row changes in some way. Make the very same change happen in the bottom row.
howItWorks: Pearson describes this as reasoning about the logical relationship between geometric shapes that change in one or more ways, across the rows and down the columns. It is a two by two grid with the bottom right box empty. This is the workhorse question type on the NNAT and the one Pearson uses in its own manual to explain the test.
parentTip: Every wrong answer on a well built analogy item follows all the rules but one. That is the key to teaching it. When your child gets one wrong, do not just give the answer. Ask which single rule that choice broke. Doing that three or four times teaches the whole question type.

questions.prompt: Make the bottom row change the same way as the top row.

figure.alt: Top row: an empty diamond, then a filled blue diamond. Bottom row: an empty triangle, then an empty box.

questions.explanation: Across the top, the empty shape becomes filled in. So the empty triangle becomes a filled triangle. Choice b never filled in and choice c changed the shape.
questions.strategy: Name the change in three words: it fills in. Then do exactly that.

questions.prompt: Finish the bottom row the same way.

figure.alt: Top row: a small empty grey tall rectangle, then a small empty grey tall rectangle. Bottom row: a small empty grey kite, then an empty box.

questions.explanation: Going across, the shape gets smaller. Choice b did not get smaller.
questions.strategy: Say the change out loud, then do exactly that to the shape below.

questions.prompt: Finish the bottom row the same way.

figure.alt: Top row: a blue slanted rectangle, then a blue slanted rectangle, turned a quarter turn. Bottom row: a blue tall rectangle, then an empty box.

questions.explanation: Going across, the shape turns a quarter turn. Choice b did not turn.
questions.strategy: Say the change out loud, then do exactly that to the shape below.

questions.prompt: Finish the bottom row the same way.

figure.alt: Top row: an empty yellow kite, then an empty yellow kite, turned a quarter turn. Bottom row: an empty yellow circle, then an empty box.

questions.explanation: Going across, the shape turns a quarter turn. Choice b did not turn.

questions.prompt: Make the bottom row change the same way.

figure.alt: Top row: a yellow square, then a green square. Bottom row: a yellow circle, then an empty box.

questions.explanation: The colour changes from yellow to green going across. The shape stays the same going down. So the answer is a green circle. Choice d used the wrong colour and choice e emptied it out.
questions.strategy: One rule across, one rule down. The answer has to obey both.

questions.prompt: Make the bottom row change the same way.

figure.alt: Top row: a small yellow star, then a big yellow star. Bottom row: a small yellow hexagon, then an empty box.

questions.explanation: The shape gets bigger going across and nothing else changes. So the small hexagon becomes a big hexagon.
questions.strategy: When only the size changes, check the colour and shape have stayed exactly the same.

questions.prompt: Finish the bottom row the same way.

figure.alt: Top row: an empty green plus sign, then a green plus sign. Bottom row: an empty green trapezoid, then an empty box.

questions.explanation: Going across, the shape fills in. Choice b never filled in.
questions.strategy: Check what changed AND what stayed the same. Both are clues.

questions.prompt: Finish the bottom row the same way.

figure.alt: Top row: a small empty yellow ring, then a big empty yellow ring. Bottom row: a small empty yellow slanted rectangle, then an empty box.

questions.explanation: Going across, the shape gets bigger. Choice b did not get bigger.

questions.prompt: Finish the bottom row the same way.

figure.alt: Top row: a green octagon, then a grey octagon. Bottom row: a green arrow, then an empty box.

questions.explanation: Going across, the color turns grey. Choice b kept the old color.

questions.prompt: Two things change. Make both happen.

figure.alt: Top row: an empty triangle, then a filled triangle turned upside down. Bottom row: an empty arrow, then an empty box.

questions.explanation: Two rules run across: the shape fills in, and it turns halfway round. Choice b filled in but did not turn. Choice c turned but did not fill in.
questions.strategy: Two rules means two checks. Go through them one at a time.

questions.prompt: Make the bottom row change the same way.

figure.alt: Top row: one blue circle, then two blue circles. Bottom row: one green square, then an empty box.

questions.explanation: One becomes two going across. So one green square becomes two green squares. Choice c has three, which is one too many.
questions.strategy: Count both boxes on the top row before you look at the answers.

questions.prompt: Finish the bottom row the same way.

questions.explanation: Two things change: the color turns green, and the shape empties out. Choice b kept the old color. Choice c stayed filled in.
questions.strategy: Two changes means two checks. Go through them one at a time.

figure.alt: Top row: a yellow wide rectangle, then a big empty yellow wide rectangle. Bottom row: a yellow hexagon, then an empty box.

questions.explanation: Two things change: the shape gets bigger, and the shape empties out. Choice b did not get bigger. Choice c stayed filled in.
questions.strategy: Two changes means two checks. Go through them one at a time.

figure.alt: Top row: a green pentagon, then the same pentagon upside down. Bottom row: a green house shape, then an empty box.

questions.prompt: Finish the bottom row the same way.

figure.alt: Top row: a small empty grey pentagon, then a small grey pentagon. Bottom row: a small empty grey slanted rectangle, then an empty box.

questions.explanation: Going across, the shape fills in. Choice b never filled in.
questions.strategy: Check what changed AND what stayed the same. Both are clues.

figure.alt: Top row: a filled blue square, then a bigger empty blue square. Bottom row: a filled green star, then an empty box.

questions.explanation: Two things happen: the shape empties out and it gets bigger. Choice b emptied but stayed small. Choice c grew but stayed filled.
questions.strategy: If two answers each do half the job, the right one does both.

figure.alt: Top row: a blue arrow pointing right, then the same arrow turned a quarter turn. Bottom row: a blue flag, then an empty box.

questions.explanation: The shape turns one quarter turn clockwise. Choices b and c turn too far or the wrong way.
questions.strategy: Turning the wrong way is the commonest slip. Settle the direction first.

questions.explanation: Two things change: the shape turns a quarter turn, and the shape fills in. Choice b did not turn. Choice c never filled in.
questions.strategy: Two changes means two checks. Go through them one at a time.

questions.prompt: Finish the bottom row the same way.

figure.alt: Top row: a green slanted rectangle, then a small green slanted rectangle, with a criss cross pattern inside. Bottom row: a green trapezoid, then an empty box.

questions.explanation: Two things change: the shape gets smaller, and the inside becomes a criss cross pattern. Choice b did not get smaller. Choice c did not become a criss cross pattern.
questions.strategy: Two changes means two checks. Go through them one at a time.

figure.alt: Top row: two medium yellow hexagons, then four small yellow hexagons. Bottom row: two medium green triangles, then an empty box.

questions.explanation: Two rules: the count doubles and each shape shrinks. Choice b doubled but stayed big. Choice c shrank but did not double.
questions.strategy: More shapes usually means smaller shapes. Watch for the trade.

questions.prompt: Finish the bottom row the same way.

figure.alt: Top row: an empty blue six-pointed star, then three empty blue six-pointed stars. Bottom row: an empty blue star, then an empty box.

questions.strategy: Say the change out loud, then do exactly that to the shape below.

figure.alt: Top row: a small empty blue slanted rectangle, then a small empty blue slanted rectangle, turned upside down. Bottom row: a small empty blue wide rectangle, then an empty box.

figure.alt: Top row: an empty yellow hexagon, then a yellow hexagon. Bottom row: an empty yellow half circle, then an empty box.

figure.alt: Top row: a striped blue circle, then a solid blue circle. Bottom row: a striped blue pentagon, then an empty box.

questions.explanation: The stripes become a solid fill. Nothing else changes. Choice d emptied the shape instead of filling it.
questions.strategy: Solid, empty, striped and dotted are four different fills. Name the one you see.

figure.alt: Top row: a small empty green arrow, then a big empty blue arrow. Bottom row: a small empty green octagon, then an empty box.

questions.explanation: Two things change: the shape gets bigger, and the color turns blue. Choice b did not get bigger. Choice c kept the old color.
questions.strategy: Check what changed AND what stayed the same. Both are clues.

figure.alt: Top row: a small empty grey triangle, then two small grey triangles, with a criss cross pattern inside. Bottom row: a small empty grey bow tie, then an empty box.

questions.explanation: Two things change: there are 2 of them instead, and the inside becomes a criss cross pattern. Choice b kept the old number. Choice c did not become a criss cross pattern.
questions.strategy: Check what changed AND what stayed the same. Both are clues.

figure.alt: Top row: a grey six-pointed star, then a small empty grey six-pointed star. Bottom row: a grey cross, then an empty box.

questions.explanation: Two things change: the shape empties out, and the shape gets smaller. Choice b stayed filled in. Choice c did not get smaller.
questions.strategy: Check what changed AND what stayed the same. Both are clues.

figure.alt: Top row: a small green kite, then a bigger green kite turned a quarter turn. Bottom row: a small green leaf, then an empty box.

questions.explanation: Grow, and turn a quarter turn clockwise. Choice b turned the wrong way and choice c did not grow.
questions.strategy: Two of the five choices usually differ only in the turn. Settle the turn, then the rest.

figure.alt: Top row: a yellow square with a dot near the top, then the same square with the dot near the bottom. Bottom row: a green circle with a dot near the top, then an empty box.

questions.explanation: The dot moves from the top to the bottom of the shape. Everything else stays put. Choice c moved it sideways instead and choice e lost it.
questions.strategy: Follow the small detail. The big shape is often just a container.

figure.alt: Top row: an empty green slanted rectangle, then a green slanted rectangle, with stripes inside and turned upside down. Bottom row: an empty green hexagon, then an empty box.

questions.explanation: Two things change: the inside becomes stripes, and the shape turns upside down. Choice b did not become stripes. Choice c did not turn.
questions.strategy: Two changes means two checks. Go through them one at a time.

figure.alt: Top row: a yellow right triangle, then an empty blue right triangle. Bottom row: a yellow star, then an empty box.

questions.explanation: Two things change: the color turns blue, and the shape empties out. Choice b kept the old color. Choice c stayed filled in.
questions.strategy: Two changes means two checks. Go through them one at a time.

figure.alt: Top row: four small blue stars, then two large blue stars. Bottom row: four small yellow diamonds, then an empty box.

questions.explanation: Halve the count and enlarge what is left. Choice b halved but stayed small. Choice c grew but kept four.
questions.strategy: Two rules that move in opposite directions: fewer and bigger.

figure.alt: Top row: a grey upside-down triangle, then a small empty green upside-down triangle. Bottom row: a grey four-pointed star, then an empty box.

questions.explanation: Three things change: the shape gets smaller, the shape empties out, and the color turns green. Choice b did not get smaller. Choice c stayed filled in.
questions.strategy: Each wrong answer follows all the rules but one. Find the one that breaks none.

figure.alt: Top row: an empty yellow six-pointed star, then a small grey six-pointed star, with a criss cross pattern inside. Bottom row: an empty yellow hexagon, then an empty box.

questions.explanation: Three things change: the color turns grey, the shape gets smaller, and the inside becomes a criss cross pattern. Choice b kept the old color. Choice c did not get smaller.
questions.strategy: Each wrong answer follows all the rules but one. Find the one that breaks none.

figure.alt: Top row: one small empty green hexagon, then three smaller filled green hexagons turned upside down. Bottom row: one small empty blue trapezoid, then an empty box.

questions.explanation: Three rules at once: the count goes from one to three, the shape fills in, and it turns upside down. Each wrong answer drops exactly one of the three.
questions.strategy: With three rules, list them on your fingers and check the answer against every finger.

figure.alt: Top row: a small blue kite, then four small blue kites, with a criss cross pattern inside. Bottom row: a small blue octagon, then an empty box.

questions.explanation: Three things change: there are 4 of them instead, the shape gets smaller, and the inside becomes a criss cross pattern. Choice b kept the old number. Choice c did not get smaller.
questions.strategy: List every change on your fingers, then test the answer against every finger.

figure.alt: Top row: a blue wide rectangle, then four small green wide rectangles. Bottom row: a blue half circle, then an empty box.

questions.explanation: Three things change: the shape gets smaller, the color turns green, and there are 4 of them instead. Choice b did not get smaller. Choice c kept the old color.
questions.strategy: List every change on your fingers, then test the answer against every finger.

figure.alt: Top row: a small grey right triangle, then a small blue right triangle. Bottom row: a small grey ring, then an empty box.

questions.explanation: Going across, the color turns blue. Choice b kept the old color.
questions.strategy: Say the change out loud, then do exactly that to the shape below.

figure.alt: Top row: a small empty blue tall rectangle, then a small blue tall rectangle, with stripes inside. Bottom row: a small empty blue pentagon, then an empty box.

questions.explanation: Going across, the inside becomes stripes. Choice b did not become stripes.
questions.strategy: Say the change out loud, then do exactly that to the shape below.

figure.alt: Top row: a grey chevron, then a yellow chevron. Bottom row: a grey half circle, then an empty box.

questions.explanation: Going across, the color turns yellow. Choice b kept the old color.
questions.strategy: Say the change out loud, then do exactly that to the shape below.

figure.alt: Top row: a solid yellow octagon, then the same octagon with a criss cross pattern. Bottom row: a solid yellow oval, then an empty box.

questions.explanation: The solid fill becomes a criss cross grid. Choice b used dots, which is a different pattern.
questions.strategy: Zoom in on the fill. Grid, dots and stripes look similar at a glance and are not the same.

figure.alt: Top row: a small yellow right triangle, then a big yellow right triangle, with flat stripes inside. Bottom row: a small yellow trapezoid, then an empty box.

questions.explanation: Two things change: the inside becomes flat stripes, and the shape gets bigger. Choice b did not become flat stripes. Choice c did not get bigger.
questions.strategy: Check what changed AND what stayed the same. Both are clues.

figure.alt: Top row: an empty blue triangle, then three blue triangles. Bottom row: an empty blue wide rectangle, then an empty box.

questions.explanation: Two things change: there are 3 of them instead, and the shape fills in. Choice b kept the old number. Choice c never filled in.
questions.strategy: Check what changed AND what stayed the same. Both are clues.

figure.alt: Top row: a green trapezoid, then a green trapezoid, with a criss cross pattern inside and turned three quarters of the way round. Bottom row: a green arrow, then an empty box.

questions.explanation: Two things change: the inside becomes a criss cross pattern, and the shape turns three quarters of the way round. Choice b did not become a criss cross pattern. Choice c did not turn.
questions.strategy: Check what changed AND what stayed the same. Both are clues.

figure.alt: Top row: a blue right triangle, then the same triangle turned three quarters of the way round. Bottom row: a green crescent, then an empty box.

questions.explanation: The shape turns three quarters of the way clockwise, which is the same as one quarter anticlockwise. Choice b turned only one quarter clockwise, the opposite way.
questions.strategy: Three quarters clockwise and one quarter anticlockwise land in the same place. Pick whichever is easier to picture.

figure.alt: Top row: a small blue hexagon, then four small blue hexagons, turned upside down. Bottom row: a small blue arrow, then an empty box.

questions.explanation: Three things change: the shape gets smaller, the shape turns upside down, and there are 4 of them instead. Choice b did not get smaller. Choice c did not turn.
questions.strategy: Two changes means two checks. Go through them one at a time.

figure.alt: Top row: a small empty green kite, then four small green kites, with stripes inside and turned a quarter turn. Bottom row: a small empty green half circle, then an empty box.

questions.explanation: Three things change: the shape turns a quarter turn, there are 4 of them instead, and the inside becomes stripes. Choice b did not turn. Choice c kept the old number.
questions.strategy: Two changes means two checks. Go through them one at a time.

figure.alt: Top row: an empty square with a small filled circle inside, then an empty circle with a small filled square inside. Bottom row: an empty triangle with a small star inside, then an empty box.

questions.explanation: The inside shape and the outside shape swap places, and each keeps its own colour. The outer one is always empty and the inner one always filled. So the star goes outside and the triangle goes inside.
questions.strategy: Swap questions are easy to spot and easy to get wrong. Check that each shape kept its own colour after the swap.

figure.alt: Top row: six small blue circles, then three medium blue circles. Bottom row: six small green squares, then an empty box.

questions.explanation: The count halves from six to three, and the shapes grow. Choice c halved twice instead of once.
questions.strategy: Halving six gives three, not two. Do the arithmetic before you look.

figure.alt: Top row: a small yellow hexagon, then two big yellow hexagons, turned upside down. Bottom row: a small yellow oval, then an empty box.

questions.explanation: Three things change: there are 2 of them instead, the shape turns upside down, and the shape gets bigger. Choice b kept the old number. Choice c did not turn.
questions.strategy: Each wrong answer follows all the rules but one. Find the one that breaks none.

figure.alt: Top row: a small empty yellow square, then three small empty grey squares. Bottom row: a small empty yellow cross, then an empty box.

questions.explanation: Three things change: the shape gets smaller, there are 3 of them instead, and the color turns grey. Choice b did not get smaller. Choice c kept the old number.
questions.strategy: Each wrong answer follows all the rules but one. Find the one that breaks none.

figure.alt: Top row: one small striped yellow chevron, then two large solid green chevrons turned a quarter turn. Bottom row: one small striped yellow bowtie, then an empty box.

questions.explanation: Four rules at once: the count doubles, the colour turns green, the stripes fill in solid, and the shape turns a quarter turn. Each wrong answer keeps three rules and breaks one.
questions.strategy: This is as hard as the NNAT gets. Write the four changes down, then test each answer against all four.

figure.alt: Top row: a blue ring, then four empty blue rings, turned three quarters of the way round. Bottom row: a blue square, then an empty box.

questions.explanation: Three things change: the shape turns three quarters of the way round, the shape empties out, and there are 4 of them instead. Choice b did not turn. Choice c stayed filled in.
questions.strategy: List every change on your fingers, then test the answer against every finger.

figure.alt: Top row: a green diamond, then a small empty green diamond, turned upside down. Bottom row: a green tall rectangle, then an empty box.

questions.explanation: Three things change: the shape turns upside down, the shape empties out, and the shape gets smaller. Choice b did not turn. Choice c stayed filled in.
questions.strategy: List every change on your fingers, then test the answer against every finger.
